text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it actually does. The goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to read, not to add new features. For example, you might break a long function into smaller parts, rename confusing variables, or remove duplicate logic. This helps reduce technical debt, which is the hidden cost of messy code that slows you down later. When you refactor regularly, your code becomes more understandable for yourself and for other developers. It is like tidying a room: you keep the same furniture, but you arrange it so you can find things quickly and move around easily.
